response: Yes, it is possible to predict which head and neck cancer survivors may develop fears of recurrence. Research has found that optimism is the strongest predictor of fear of recurrence, independent of anxiety and the level of fear reported prior to treatment. Additionally, components of the cognitive and emotional representations, as well as coping strategies, are also associated with fears of recurrence. Therefore, assessing a patient's level of optimism and other psychological factors can help healthcare providers identify those who may be at higher risk of developing fears of recurrence and provide targeted support and interventions to address these concerns.
